DO NOT AUDIT LEAN DECLARATION EXISTENCE WITH A REGEX -- use the graph; three false conclusions in one session came from this

The pattern, which cost me and two subagents real time in run 0054 s0010 and will recur: you
want to know whether a \lean{Name} pin resolves, or whether a declaration exists, so you grep
for '^(theorem|lemma|def|instance) Name'. That regex is wrong in at least three ways, all of
which occur in AJC:

  1. ATTRIBUTE PREFIX. The declaration is written  @[simp] lemma sectionsCast_refl ...  so the
     keyword is not at line start. This produced SIX false "pin does not resolve" findings on
     Picard_SectionGradedRing.tex nodes whose pins are in fact fine.
  2. UNIVERSE-BINDER SUFFIX ON THE NAME. Written  theorem toSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits.{v', u', w'} ...
     so the identifier is followed by ".{" rather than whitespace. Exactly four declarations in
     AJC use this. Horizon's own graph scanner has the SAME bug (filed as I-0452), so here the
     regex and the tool are wrong together -- the worst case, because agreement looks like
     confirmation.
  3. NAMESPACE CONTEXT. A bare name says nothing about the fully-qualified name; you must find
     the enclosing namespace/end block, and an "open" can make the source text differ from the
     pin.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, in increasing order of authority:
  - horizon graph -p PROJECT get decl:Fully.Qualified.Name    -- resolves, or says "no node
    matching". Same index the DAG is built from.
  - horizon graph -p PROJECT sync --blueprint TEX --lean DIR  -- read its warnings; this is the
    definitive list of unresolved pins and it cross-checks every pin at once.
  - horizon search NAME  -- spans all projects AND mathlib, which a grep cannot.
  - A scratch file with  #print axioms Fully.Qualified.Name  under lake env lean -- the only
    check that is not a text search at all, and the one that settles both existence and whether
    the thing is proved.

THE GENERALISABLE POINT, beyond Lean: when auditing a CLAIM about the codebase, prefer the tool
that owns the index over a pattern you wrote in the moment -- and when the two disagree, find

**TRIMMED 2026-07-27 (janitor hygiene pass, run 0054 s0010).** This item was written as a frontier record and was WRONG TWICE IN THE SAME DIRECTION within one day — "the gate needs FOUR statements", then "there is deliberately no `instance : HasRigidPushforward`". Per this item's own meta-lesson and `I-0439`'s corollary, the state half is now deleted rather than corrected a third time: **the gate's status lives in roadmap row `AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward`** (done, pinned `02ae27824`/`744a74bf2`), which is the artifact designed to be re-set. What is kept below is the mathematics and the tooling, which do not go stale.

**HOW ℙ¹ INTEGRALITY FELL — the durable template.** Not by cohomology. Identify the chart section rings as polynomial rings, $\Gamma(\mathbb{P}^1_k, D_+(X_i)) \simeq_{alg[k]} k[T]$: the tree already had the *spanning* half (`span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/P1ChartData.lean`), and the missing half was **injectivity**, obtained from the section-ring pushout — $V_0$ is the fibre product of the affine $D_+(X_0)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb{Z}[X_0,X_1]$ with $\operatorname{Spec} k$, so mathlib's `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen` presents $\Gamma(V_0)$ as a `CommRingCat` pushout and `IsPushout.desc` yields a retraction. Then "both chart rings are domains" gives integrality by `IsReduced.of_openCover` plus density of the overlap. Reusable wherever a hand-built projective object needs a ring-level identification.

**WHY THE DISCHARGE WAS BELIEVABLE, and this is the part to copy.** Measure at the **SYNTHESIS SITE**, not at the theorem: restate the consumers *without* the `[HasRigidPushforward C]` binder, so Lean must synthesize the gate to elaborate them, and read `#print axioms` there. The same measurement applied to `HasPicScheme` is what exposes `instHasPicScheme` as poisoned. Non-vacuity is a separate question again, and needs a witness object (`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Witness.lean` exhibits ℙ¹ satisfying all three binders). Catalogue of what each check does and does not see: `I-0442`.

**THREE TOOLING GOTCHAS, in descending order of reuse:**

1. `lake env lean <file>` does **not** run this project's style linters (`linter.style.maxHeartbeats`, `linter.style.setOption`). A file can be silent under `lake env lean` and still warn under `lake build <module>`. Always finish a new module with a single-module `lake build` (~20-35 s warm) before calling it warning-free. Never run a bare `lake build` (43 min — see `I-0319`).
2. The direct route to the chart identification through `HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective` **`isDefEq`-times-out** at the concrete grading — write it `Away.mk`-first.
3. Mathlib v4.31 still has **no** integrality/irreducibility/reducedness API for `Proj` at all, while it has all three for affine space (`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean:392/402/419`). Do not go looking; the pushout route above is why this was closable anyway.
